pass_rule: all core questions substantially correct in the learner's own words; stretch questions inform the grade, not the gate

questions.prompt: You run `go mod init github.com/you/weather` in an empty folder. What does the go.mod it creates say, and what gets added to it later as the project grows?
expected_points: go mod init creates go.mod with the module path and the Go version
the module path is the module's globally unique name and the root of all its import paths
require lines are added later, recording each dependency and its exact version

questions.prompt: How does Go decide which names in a package are usable from other packages? Why would you deliberately keep a function unexported?
expected_points: capitalized first letter = exported, lowercase = unexported; there is no public/private keyword
the compiler rejects references to unexported names from outside the package
unexported helpers stay free to change; every export is a commitment to callers

questions.prompt: Your module is `tutor.local/packages-modules` and you add a folder `report/`. What import line does main.go need, and what prefix do you use to call its functions?
expected_points: import path = module path + folder path: tutor.local/packages-modules/report
after importing you use the package name, the last segment: report.Line(...)
one folder = one package; all its files share the package name

questions.prompt: You import an external package like `rsc.io/quote` and `go run .` refuses. What does running `go mod tidy` do to fix it, and what does it change on disk?
expected_points: tidy scans source imports, downloads missing modules, and rewrites go.mod to match
it adds require lines for used dependencies and removes lines for unused ones
go.sum gains checksums so everyone builds with identical dependency code

questions.prompt: The exercise tests declare `package temperature_test` instead of `package temperature`. What difference does that make to what the tests can touch?
expected_points: an external test package can only use exported names
so the tests exercise exactly the surface real importers see

questions.prompt: Why do real-world module paths look like URLs (`github.com/you/project`) instead of short names like `project`?
expected_points: the path must be globally unique so imports are unambiguous
it doubles as the location the toolchain fetches the module from
local-only modules like tutor.local/... work because they are never fetched
